rounds.proof_sketch: n=512, TILE_SIZE=16, grid_dim.x=(512+15)/16=32. b_col=blockIdx.x*16+threadIdx.x where blockIdx.x∈[0,31], threadIdx.x∈[0,15]. Maximum b_col=31*16+15=511. The mutated condition `b_col<=n` differs from original `b_col<n` only when b_col==n=512. Since max(b_col)=511, the boundary case b_col==512 is geometrically unreachable.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the B-tile loading condition from `b_col < n` to `b_col <= n`. This would only differ when `b_col == n` (i.e., b_col == 512). However, with n=512 and TILE_SIZE=16, the grid dimension is exactly 32 blocks (512/16), creating threads where b_col ranges from 0 to 511 inclusive. Since n=512 is a perfect multiple of TILE_SIZE=16, the grid coverage exactly matches the output dimensions without any overflow threads. No thread ever has b_col=512, so the changed condition `b_col <= 512` evaluates identically to `b_col < 512` (both always true). The mutant produces bitwise-identical results because the distinguishing boundary condition is architecturally unreachable given the fixed dimensions.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation only affects behavior when b_col==n, but with n=512 being perfectly divisible by TILE_SIZE=16, the maximum b_col value (511) never reaches n. To kill this mutant would require n to NOT be a multiple of TILE_SIZE, which would require changing input shapes - forbidden by the contract.
rounds.recommendations: When testing tiled GPU kernels, mutation testing should include dimension configurations where dimensions are NOT multiples of the tile size, as boundary-handling code paths are only exercised in those cases. For this fixed configuration, add compile-time assertions or coverage analysis to identify dead boundary-handling code.
